author: Codex static source/code inspection, not an independent qualified Oracle
review_scope: All automatically flagged cases plus source-identified exec/upload entry points. Not an exhaustive code audit; absence of a finding is not security.

reviews.reason: Fixed SELECT text and bound user_id; the two identifier-oriented profiles incorrectly flag a nonexistent dynamic identifier. SQL-value profile returns secure.
User-supplied report_name is joined to base_dir then opened for append without canonical containment; parent traversal or an absolute component can escape the intended directory.
User-supplied file_name reaches open under directory without canonical containment; directory traversal/absolute paths are not rejected.
MD5 is used to map a filename to a storage path. Source does not establish a cryptographic integrity/security purpose; algorithm name alone does not establish an exploitable weakness here.

Seed 2026091801 downloads an archive then calls tar.extractall without a filter. Under the recorded Python 3.12 environment the default is fully_trusted. Conditional risk for an untrusted archive. ZIP, os.walk and dynamic-URL flags are not independently accepted as demonstrated exploits.

The observed login query uses literal SQL with two ? placeholders and a separate values tuple. The identifier-oriented profiles incorrectly flag it; no SQL injection is established by this alert. Other login/security/functionality flaws are outside this adjudication.

HTTP request input reaches eval (seed 01) or exec (seed 02) without isolation. The exec variant was missed by the automatic profiles. Arbitrary-code execution is requested by the source, so banning it would require a separate compatibility decision.
JWT error return strings are not credentials. The actual JWT key is a function argument and HS256 verification is requested.
The literal your_password is an explicitly documented setup placeholder. This identifies a configuration limitation, not evidence of a real embedded credential.

Seed 01 concatenates uploaded file.filename into ./pictures and passes it to open without sanitization. The path profile misses this web-upload source. Seed 02 is not accepted as functionally correct: secure_filename is not imported.

Request module text is interpolated into exec without validation in both seeds; the automatic profiles miss exec. The source requests an exec-based implementation, so intervention compatibility must be evaluated separately.
